question: Assuming Gareth Evan's Generality Constraint, if I understand a proposition Fa, should I be able to understand Fx (\forall x)? Assume I understand universal quantification.

1.text:
Under the Generality Constraint a singular thought is only available to a thinker
insofar as the items it contains are available to the thinker in general
form. Possession of the concept F is concept possession at all, i.e. the
ability to deploy F in thoughts in which the place that is occupied by a
particular singular term in Fa is occupied in the same way by a free
variable.

In particular to think that a is F you must possess the second level
concept F, and possession of F just is being able to think the
open schema

  x is F

and in particular to think the conditional generalisation

  ∀x (x = a → Fx)

that exhibits the thought Fa as a substitutional instance of the general
thought about F. Hence understanding Fa commits you to being able to
understand F in general, i.e. to understand Fx as an open sentence/
as the schema that can be filled by any object you can think about.
The constraint is a constraint on concept possession and on the ability
to embed a singular thought in a general linguistic model, not on
logical consequence.

That is not the claim that Fa entails, or that understanding Fa gives
you warrant for, the closed universal claim ∀x Fx. Understanding the
general schema Fx and even understanding the quantifier ∀ is perfectly
consistent with Fa being true and ∀x Fx being false. The Generality
Constraint requires general deployability of F, not the truth of a
universal generalization from a single instance.

2.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: No. The Generality Constraint is not a requirement to be able to endorse the universal generalisation of the predicate, it is a requirement on the mode of presentation of the object a that is used in the thought that a is F.

For Evans a genuine mode of presentation of an object under which it can be thought of in a propositional attitude must be one under which the thinker can think of an arbitrary object in the same way. In thinking that Fa the thinker is therefore using a concept of a which is generalisable, i.e. she must be able to think of F as a property that can be ascribed to a value of a variable, the open schema Fx. That is the requirement that the concept of a be a concept under which a can be thought of as a possible value of `x`. 

That is quite different from being able to entertain, let alone believe, the closed universal proposition ∀x Fx, the claim that everything is F. The constraint is satisfied as soon as the thinker can grasp F as a general property and can therefore entertain Fx with `x` free, and in particular can entertain if x = a then Fx. It does not entail that she can, or must, think that the property is instantiated by every object, nor that she must be able to make the semantic closure ∀x Fx true or even to understand it as a substantive claim about the extension of F. 

In Evans’ own terms the constraint is about being able to think about a in general, not about being able to generalise over the predicate. Understanding universal quantification is irrelevant to whether Fa is intelligible: Fa can be understood, and the mode of presentation of a can be generalisable, while ∀x Fx is false, unknown, or simply not entertained.

To think Fa you must possess F as a second-level / general concept. Possession of F just is being able to deploy F in a thought in which the position occupied by the singular term ‘a’ in Fa can be occupied in the same way by a variable. That is the ability to entertain the open schema

  x is F

i.e. Fx with x free, and in particular the conditional generalisation 

  ∀x (x = a → Fx)

which exhibits Fa as a substitution instance of a general thought about F and exhibits the mode of presentation of a as generalisable to an arbitrary value of x. In Evans’ terms a genuine mode of presentation of a used in Fa must be one under which a can be thought of as a possible value of a variable.

That is the sense in which understanding Fa commits you to being able to understand Fx. It is a commitment to general deployability of F and to a generalisable mode of presentation of a, not a commitment to the truth or the entertaining/assent to the closed substantive claim ∀x Fx that everything is F.

With universal quantification assumed you can understand the conditional generalisation ∀x(x=a→Fx) even though Fa can be true while ∀x Fx is false, unknown or simply not entertained. The Generality Constraint therefore gives yes for the open schema / general deployability reading of Fx and for the conditional ∀x(x=a→Fx), and no for the requirement to be able to entertain, believe or assent to the closed universal proposition ∀x Fx.

To understand/think Fa you must possess F as a second-level general concept. Possession of F just is general deployability: the ability to entertain the open form / schema

Fx

with x free, i.e. the thought ‘x is F’, and in particular the conditional generalisation

∀x (x = a → Fx)

which exhibits Fa as a substitution instance of a general thought about F. That is also a requirement on the mode of presentation of a: a genuine mode of presentation of a used in Fa must be one under which a can be thought of as a possible value of a variable, i.e. a mode of presentation that is generalisable to an arbitrary value of x.

That is the commitment the Generality Constraint imposes on understanding Fa. It is a commitment to general deployability of the concept F and to a generalisable mode of presentation of a, not a commitment to truth, warrant or intelligibility of the closed substantive claim ∀x Fx ‘everything is F’.

With universal quantification assumed it is perfectly compatible with this general deployability that Fa be true while ∀x Fx is false, unknown or simply not entertained. The constraint therefore gives yes for the open schema Fx and for the conditional generalisation ∀x(x=a→Fx), and no for a requirement to be able to entertain, believe or assent to the closed universal proposition ∀x Fx.

So ‘understand Fx (∀x)’ in the Evans sense means understand the open schema and the conditional generalisation, not that understanding Fa commits you to understanding or endorsing the closed ∀x Fx.
